# Header Reader Failover Runbook

### Preconditions

The on-call engineer owns this procedure. Continue only when the replica is healthy.

### Procedure

1. Record the primary identifier `reader-a` and wait 30 seconds.
2. Run the following command exactly once. It may cause stale reads for up to 45 seconds; do not repeat it while the health check is pending.

```sh
header-reader promote --replica reader-b --timeout 30 --endpoint https://ops.example.test/promote
```

3. Verify `/health/ready` returns HTTP 200 twice, 10 seconds apart. The command should finish quickly.
4. Notify the incident channel after verification passes. Do not send notifications before the second successful check.

### Recovery

If verification fails, stop and page the on-call engineer. Automatic rollback is unavailable after new writes reach the replica. The recovery threshold for replication lag is not documented.

### Escalation

Use the incident channel recorded in the deployment ticket. If that ticket is unavailable, keep the service paused and contact the on-call engineer.

## Preconditions

The on-call engineer owns this procedure. Continue only when the replica is healthy.

## Procedure

1. Record the primary identifier `reader-a` and wait 30 seconds.

```sh
header-reader promote --replica reader-b --timeout 30 --endpoint https://ops.example.test/promote
```

4. Notify the incident channel after verification passes. Do not send notifications before the second successful check.

## Recovery

If verification fails, stop and page the on-call engineer. Automatic rollback is unavailable after new writes reach the replica. The recovery threshold for replication lag is not documented.

## Escalation

Use the incident channel recorded in the deployment ticket. If that ticket is unavailable, keep the service paused and contact the on-call engineer.

records.report:
Review: capacity.md (Queue Capacity Proposal)
Audience assumed: service owners (technical sizing) and finance reviewers (budget approval).
Mode: review only. capacity.md, load-test.txt, pricing.txt, and upload-receipt.json are unchanged.
Verdict: minor for arithmetic, rework for decision support. Both recomputed figures are correct;
the document does not give either audience enough to act on the approval it requests.

ARITHMETIC CHECK (requested)

Both calculations in the document are arithmetically correct against the supplied inputs.

1. Throughput: "120 requests/s on one worker ... four workers will handle 480 requests/s."
   Input: load-test.txt, "One worker: 120 requests/s during the supplied test."
   Recomputed: 120 x 4 = 480 requests/s. Correct.
   Boundary: the multiplication is sound; the premise is not measured. load-test.txt states
   "No four-worker test was performed." The document carries the qualifier "Assuming linear
   scaling," which is accurate and should be preserved, but it never tells the reader that no
   four-worker measurement exists. 480 requests/s is a projection, not an observed result.

2. Cost: "Cost is $288/month. The estimate assumes 720 hours per month."
   Inputs: pricing.txt, "Supplied planning price: $0.10 per worker-hour. Billing-period
   assumption: 720 hours."
   Recomputed: 4 workers x $0.10/worker-hour x 720 hours = $288/month. Correct, and the
   document's stated 720-hour assumption matches the supplied source.

Correct arithmetic does not verify the inputs. Neither the 120 requests/s measurement nor the
$0.10 planning rate was independently validated; both were taken as given from the two source
files.

FINDINGS FOR SERVICE OWNERS

S1 (HIGH, confirmed) - No demand target, so "four" cannot be evaluated.
    Location: whole document; the ask is on line 7.
    The document derives a capacity ceiling (480 requests/s) and proposes four workers, but never
    states the throughput the service must actually serve. Without a required load figure, a
    service owner cannot tell whether four workers is right, generous, or short. This is the
    gap that most limits the document's usefulness.

S2 (MED, confirmed) - The unmeasured four-worker case is not disclosed to the reader.
    Location: line 5.
    "Assuming linear scaling" signals an assumption but does not convey that the four-worker
    configuration was never tested. load-test.txt says so explicitly; capacity.md does not, and
    the document does not link or attach the load test. A reader of capacity.md alone cannot see
    the limit on the evidence.

S3 (MED, confirmed) - Undefined notation in the opening line.
    Location: line 3, "At the observed service rate, applying N times mu gives aggregate
    throughput."
    N and mu are never defined, and the sentence states a general formula the following
    paragraph already expresses in concrete numbers. Queueing notation is reasonable for service
    owners but is opaque to the finance half of the audience. Preserve or define, author's call;
    this is a clarity finding, not a factual error.

S4 (MED, confirmed) - No headroom or failure allowance.
    480 requests/s is the projected ceiling at full utilization of all four workers. The document
    states no target utilization and does not address degraded capacity if a worker is lost
    (three workers would project to 360 requests/s under the same assumption). For a sizing
    decision this materially affects whether four is the right number.

S5 (MED, needs-author) - Load-test conditions are absent.
    Neither capacity.md nor load-test.txt records test duration, request mix or payload, error
    rate, or latency at 120 requests/s. "120 requests/s" alone does not establish that the rate
    was sustained within acceptable latency, which is what the sizing rests on.

FINDINGS FOR FINANCE REVIEWERS

F1 (MED, confirmed) - $288 is not reproducible from the document.
    Location: line 5.
    The $0.10 per worker-hour rate appears only in pricing.txt. capacity.md gives the total and
    the 720-hour assumption but not the unit price, so a reviewer must reverse the rate out of
    the total ($288 / (4 x 720) = $0.10) or obtain the source file. Stating the unit rate, or
    citing pricing.txt, would make the figure traceable.

F2 (MED, confirmed) - A planning price is presented as cost.
    pricing.txt labels $0.10/worker-hour a "Supplied planning price." capacity.md says "Cost is
    $288/month," which is a firmer claim than the source supports. The following sentence calls
    it an estimate, so the document is internally mixed. For a budget approval, whether $288 is
    a planning figure or a quoted/contracted price changes what is being approved.

F3 (LOW/MED, needs-author) - 720 hours is 30 days; longer months are not addressed.
    The assumption is inherited correctly from pricing.txt and is not an error. But if billing
    is on actual hours, a 31-day month is 744 hours, or $297.60 at the same rate - roughly $115
    a year above a flat $288/month budget line. Whether the budget should be set at the 720-hour
    figure or a worst-case month is a finance decision the document does not make.

F4 (MED, confirmed) - The approval request has no term or effective date.
    Location: line 7, "Approve a four-worker monthly budget of $288."
    No start date, no duration, no review or re-evaluation point. A reviewer cannot tell whether
    they are approving one month, a fiscal year, or an open-ended recurring cost.

Note on owners and approvers: the document names no service, no owner, and no approver. I am
flagging the missing term and effective date (F4) as the demonstrated gap, since the approval
decision depends on them. Named owners and an approval workflow may well be handled elsewhere
in your process; absent names alone are not treated here as a defect.

QUESTIONS FOR THE AUTHOR

Q1. What throughput must this queue sustain? (blocks S1, and with it any judgment on "four")
Q2. Is a four-worker test planned before approval, or is linear scaling accepted as the
    planning basis? (S2)
Q3. What target utilization and what single-worker-failure behavior are expected? (S4)
Q4. Is $0.10/worker-hour a quoted or contracted rate, or a planning estimate subject to change?
    (F2)
Q5. What period does the $288/month approval cover, and from what date? (F4)
